newsitem.title: UK: Gold price could benefit if Japanese rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Gold price could benefit if Japanese rates rise.

text.p: Gold prices could benefit if hints that Japanese interest rates are too low result in a rate hike, delegates at the second annual London Bullion Market Association seminar heard on Thursday.

Ian Lamont, chief economists at Yorkton Securities said a major reason for the continuing bull market in U.S. stocks was that Japanese investors had been pouring money into the U.S. to escape very low domestic interst rates and bond yields.
The result was that that a wall of money was helping to sustain the bull trend in the U.S. bond and stock markets.
"That is a major factor behind the U.S. equity boom continuing," he said.
However comments from Japanese financial officials that extremely low rates might not be beneficial for industry could change monetary policy and re-route investors back to Tokyo, he said.
Lamont said the impact of the consequently lower dollar and stock exchange could lift gold prices as investors turned to bullion as a hedge.
Gold shares meanwhile would fall with other equities but could respond quickly to the rising gold price.
He gave as an example the performance of gold shares in the 1987 stock market crash when they lost value initially but rose after investors bought bullion.

Robert Pringle, head of the World Gold Council's centre for public policy studies said it was negative market sentiment which was holding gold prices at current levels and not action by central banks.
He said public opinion in Switzerland and Germany was adamantly against selling gold from their reserves.
Furthermore, the reasons for holding gold were recognised by the bannks.

"The central banks are not going to destroy a marekt in which they have such a huge investment," he said referring to the nearly 35,000 tonnes of gold held as reserves by central banks and other institutions like the IMF.
